collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE IX: REPAIR, FAIRNESS AND MANY FUTURES (LCI-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
From the owner's Volume V concepts (401-500), the 30 themes and the five deeper subjects: old wrongs and their repair, who is heard, prejudice and fairness, care for minds and bodies, animals and hard tradeoffs, inventions and bad inventions, family life, and an island that keeps choosing its own future.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: A capable villager is never chosen as an apprentice because of the family they come from: take them on, or ask the others why.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (friend) has asked every craft master in the village to take (friend.him/her) on, and every one has said no. Everyone knows why, though nobody says it: (friend.his/her) father was a troublemaker, long ago. (subject), the master healer, has watched (friend) work. (friend.He/she) is good. What should (subject) do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) takes (friend) as an apprentice. Some people mutter. (friend) works harder than any apprentice (subject) has ever had. Within two years, the muttering has stopped.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) asks the other masters, at the gathering, to say why they refused. Nobody can give a reason that is not about (friend)'s father. It is uncomfortable. Two masters change their minds. (friend) chooses carving.
